tools.name: context_run
tools.description: Run one capability now. Saved goal:<slug> capabilities re-plan against the current environment, heal API changes and repeat their stored result checks and independent witnesses. Returns output, timing, receipt, verification and witness evidence. Optional predicates add checks; they never remove stored checks. A failed call to a learned API re-reads its contract once and retries the same operation if the API moved; an id that re-learning pointed at a different operation remains refused; caller acknowledgement cannot authorise the change. Large outputs: pass view to get a count, field projection or slice instead of the whole payload.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

fields.description: Project each element onto these paths, e.g. ["accession","sequence.length"].

tools.name: context_compose
tools.description: Give what you have and the type you want; RightClick X discovers routes across the environment and (with run:true) executes, checks and repairs them. Currency/unit refinements require explicit conversions. Attach witnesses for independent business-outcome checks. publish saves a stable goal:<slug> capability another AI can discover with context_graph and invoke with context_run; its checks survive restart and API changes. A successful multi-step pipeline is also saved for reuse.

have.description: Named inputs, e.g. {"place":"Lisbon","language":"es"} or {"x":{"type":"url","value":"https://..."}}. With publish, {"to":{"value":"EUR","fixed":true}} pins an input inside the published goal instead of making it a parameter of its API.

intent.description: Words describing the goal, e.g. 'weather forecast translated'.

witnesses.description: Independent outcome checks, repeated for every saved invocation. Discover a read-only checker in the environment. Example: [{"capability":"<checker id>","args":{"order_id":{"input":"order_id"},"tax_amount":{"output":""}},"verify":[{"op":"equals","path":"valid","value":true}]}]. input paths read this invocation's have values; output paths read the candidate result (empty string = whole result); value supplies a literal. output.description: Path in the candidate output; empty string selects all of it.

confirm.description: Required to run plans containing destructive capabilities.

tools.name: context_run
tools.description: Run one capability now. Saved goal:<slug> capabilities re-plan against the current environment, heal API changes and repeat their stored result checks and independent witnesses. Returns output, timing, receipt, verification and witness evidence. Optional predicates add checks; they never remove stored checks. A failed call to a learned API re-reads its contract once and retries the same operation if the API moved; an id that re-learning pointed at a different operation remains refused; caller acknowledgement cannot authorise the change. Large outputs: pass view to get a count, field projection or slice instead of the whole payload.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

tools.name: context_compose
tools.description: Give what you have and the type you want; RightClick X discovers routes across the environment and (with run:true) executes, checks and repairs them. Currency/unit refinements require explicit conversions. Attach witnesses for independent business-outcome checks. publish saves a stable goal:<slug> capability another AI can discover with context_graph and invoke with context_run; its checks survive restart and API changes. A successful multi-step pipeline is also saved for reuse.

have.description: Named inputs, e.g. {"place":"Lisbon","language":"es"} or {"x":{"type":"url","value":"https://..."}}. With publish, {"to":{"value":"EUR","fixed":true}} pins an input inside the published goal instead of making it a parameter of its API.

want.description: Desired semantic type, e.g. text, language, geo.lat, html, hash.

intent.description: Words describing the goal, e.g. 'weather forecast translated'.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

witnesses.description: Independent outcome checks, repeated for every saved invocation. Discover a read-only checker in the environment. Example: [{"capability":"<checker id>","args":{"order_id":{"input":"order_id"},"tax_amount":{"output":""}},"verify":[{"op":"equals","path":"valid","value":true}]}]. input paths read this invocation's have values; output paths read the candidate result (empty string = whole result); value supplies a literal. The checker must be a separate provider and must pass its predicates. Its contract is pinned on save; a changed checker fails closed.

output.description: Path in the candidate output; empty string selects all of it.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

confirm.description: Required to run plans containing destructive capabilities.

publish.description: After a successful run, save this goal as goal:<slug> in the graph AND as /x/<slug> in the synthesized API. Checks and witnesses are retained and re-run on every invocation. Stored predicates make a goal "checked"; an independent witness makes it "verified".

acquire.description: If nothing in the graph can do it: research public directories (APIs.guru, MCP Registry), learn the best candidates and re-plan.

through.description: Anchors: capability ids or search phrases the pipeline must pass through; the planner wires the types between them.

risks.description: Optional constraint: plan only with these risk labels, e.g. ["read"].

require.description: Required information the result must carry, e.g. ["resolution"] or ["gene name"]. tools.name: context_run
tools.description: Run one capability now. Saved goal:<slug> capabilities re-plan against the current environment, heal API changes and repeat their stored result checks and independent witnesses. Returns output, timing, receipt, verification and witness evidence. Optional predicates add checks; they never remove stored checks. A failed call to a learned API re-reads its contract once and retries the same operation if the API moved; an id that re-learning pointed at a different operation remains refused; caller acknowledgement cannot authorise the change. Large outputs: pass view to get a count, field projection or slice instead of the whole payload.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

fields.description: Project each element onto these paths, e.g. ["accession","sequence.length"].

count.description: Return only the number of elements, keys or characters of the selected value.

full.description: Return the selected value whole, even when it is over the response budget.

view.description: What to return of the output: a count, a projection or a slice. Without a view, an output over 32000 characters of JSON is withheld whole (never cut) and summarised by size, count and shape. The run record and receipt digest always cover the full output.

tools.name: context_compose
tools.description: Give what you have and the type you want; RightClick X discovers routes across the environment and (with run:true) executes, checks and repairs them. Currency/unit refinements require explicit conversions. Attach witnesses for independent business-outcome checks. publish saves a stable goal:<slug> capability another AI can discover with context_graph and invoke with context_run; its checks survive restart and API changes. A successful multi-step pipeline is also saved for reuse.

have.description: Named inputs, e.g. {"place":"Lisbon","language":"es"} or {"x":{"type":"url","value":"https://..."}}. With publish, {"to":{"value":"EUR","fixed":true}} pins an input inside the published goal instead of making it a parameter of its API.

want.description: Desired semantic type, e.g. text, language, geo.lat, html, hash.

intent.description: Words describing the goal, e.g. 'weather forecast translated'.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

witnesses.description: Independent outcome checks, repeated for every saved invocation. Discover a read-only checker in the environment. Example: [{"capability":"<checker id>","args":{"order_id":{"input":"order_id"},"tax_amount":{"output":""}},"verify":[{"op":"equals","path":"valid","value":true}]}]. input paths read this invocation's have values; output paths read the candidate result (empty string = whole result); value supplies a literal. The checker must be a separate provider and must pass its predicates. Its contract is pinned on save; a changed checker fails closed.

output.description: Path in the candidate output; empty string selects all of it.

verify.description: Outcome checks on the result, e.g. [{"op":"contains","value":"Lisbon"}, {"op":"gt","path":"temperature","value":-50}]. ops: exists, equals, contains, matches, type, gt, lt, length_gt. Passing them makes a result "checked"; only an independent witness makes it "verified".

confirm.description: Required to run plans containing destructive capabilities.

publish.description: After a successful run, save this goal as goal:<slug> in the graph AND as /x/<slug> in the synthesized API. Checks and witnesses are retained and re-run on every invocation. Stored predicates make a goal "checked"; an independent witness makes it "verified".

acquire.description: If nothing in the graph can do it: research public directories (APIs.guru, MCP Registry), learn the best candidates and re-plan.

through.description: Anchors: capability ids or search phrases the pipeline must pass through; the planner wires the types between them.

risks.description: Optional constraint: plan only with these risk labels, e.g. ["read"].

require.description: Required information the result must carry, e.g. ["resolution"] or ["gene name"]. Plans are judged by the fields their result declares and by how each join is supported; only an established plan runs, otherwise the outcome says unavailable/unverified and nothing runs. After running, the output is checked for every term.

origins.description: Optional egress policy, e.g. ["https://api.example.com"]: use only capabilities that send data to these origins, now and in every automatic repair. Saved with publish.

have.description: Named inputs, e.g. {"place":"Lisbon","language":"es"} or {"x":{"type":"url","value":"https://..."}}. With publish, {"to":{"value":"EUR","fixed":true}} pins an input inside the published goal instead of making it a parameter of its API.

witnesses.description: Independent outcome checks, repeated for every saved invocation. Discover a read-only checker in the environment. Example: [{"capability":"<checker id>","args":{"order_id":{"input":"order_id"},"tax_amount":{"output":""}},"verify":[{"op":"equals","path":"valid","value":true}]}]. input paths read this invocation's have values; output paths read the candidate result (empty string = whole result); value supplies a literal. output.description: Path in the candidate output; empty string selects all of it.
